extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / Royal Society readers; scientists working on anatomy, acoustics, magnetism and mathematical theory
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing early-modern natural philosophy research reports (empirical anatomy, experimental acoustics, magnetism, and mathematical exposition) for adequacy of observation, experiment, reasoning, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed anatomical description of structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a careful, part-by-part description of the nature and structure of anatomical features (e.g., periosteum, bones, pores, marrow, cartilages, mucilaginous glands, teeth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe origins and types of fibers, membranes and glandular arrangements; note surfaces, cavities, plates/laminae, fasciculi, and vascular supply; indicate how plates/strings/laminae form larger bone structures and note differences between bone, cartilage and teeth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking structure to function
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the uses and functions of anatomical parts (e.g., periosteum conveys spirits/nutrition, medullary oil lubricates joints, cartilages impart flexible strength).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect microstructure to physiological role (nutrition, lubrication, protection, flexibility, motion); enumerate distinct functions (e.g., limit growth, fasten tendons, prevent attrition) rather than merely describing form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of observational and experimental evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims by direct observation and by experiments (e.g., coagulation of mucilage with acids; monochord/string experiments for acoustics; repeated compass observations for magnetism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report experimental procedure and empirical findings plainly; give examples and results (tables, figures, numerical measures) so readers can judge the strength of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrable, reproducible experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include simple experiments or demonstrations the reader can reproduce (e.g., placing paper on string to see vibration nodes; touching string with thumb to produce trumpet-marine notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe apparatus, placements (stops/frets), and what to observe (locations of greatest motion, pricked/imperfect notes) so others can repeat and verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical reasoning and explicit proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear numerical examples and proportional reasoning to derive conclusions (e.g., harmonic ratios in monochord, species of infinite magnitude, proportions of infinite areas/solids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show calculations (e.g., monochord of 720 parts, halves/thirds producing specific notes), relate geometric analogies (line/plane/solid) and provide the proportional relationships that underpin qualitative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diagrams and tabular presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Present figures and tables to display experimental data and conceptual relationships (e.g., table of trumpet notes, figures of string vibration modes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label pricked/imperfect notes, mark positions on strings/monochord, and include sketches showing modes of vibration or geometric partitions to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and clear definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and classify distinct kinds within the topic (e.g., three species of infinite quantity; two sorts of mucilaginous glands; types of bone pores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear criteria that distinguish each class and explain analogies (line : plane : solid) so that the reader can understand the taxonomy used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose mechanistic hypotheses consistent with observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer hypotheses that account for the observed phenomena and are physically plausible (e.g., Halley's internal moving magnet/nucleus to explain secular changes in needle variation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure hypotheses explain the full set of observations and avoid proposing mechanisms that would produce impossible side-effects; show how the hypothesis resolves prior difficulties and state its implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implausible or contradictory mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject or criticise hypotheses that would entail implausible consequences (e.g., large motions of Earth's solid parts that would alter its centre of gravity and rotation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly reason about mechanical/physical consequences (centre of gravity, diurnal rotation, inundations) and prefer mechanisms that respect known constraints of the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile comparative and historical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather and compare observations across times and places (e.g., needle variation records from London, Paris, Cape d'Agulhas, St. Helena, Cape Comorin) to reveal trends and changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological tables or cited measurements spanning years/centuries; use geographic comparisons to support claims of gradual, universal change versus local irregularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for local irregularities and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and try to explain deviations from general trends (e.g., local magnetic anomalies due to unequal distribution of magnetic matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit anomalous data; propose secondary causes (irregular distribution in external shell) and explain how they modify but do not overturn the general hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect experimental findings to natural-philosophical consequences or applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate laboratory/observational results to natural phenomena or medical conditions (e.g., coagulation of mucilage explaining gout/tophaceous matter; lubrication explaining joint health).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain causal chains from experiment to condition, and show how experimental chemistry/physiology bears on disease generation and possible remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly state limitations and need for further data
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize where observations are insufficient to decide between alternatives (e.g., lack of observations in the Pacific to determine larger magnetic pattern).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out geographic or temporal gaps, indicate where future observations would be decisive, and avoid overclaiming beyond the available evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive corollaries and logical consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: From established premises and experiments, deduce corollaries (e.g., spacing of trumpet notes decreases geometrically; consequences of aliquot divisions of string).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit deductions and show how they follow from prior ratios/observations; use such corollaries to predict additional measurable phenomena.
